---
title: "wrapped"
subtitle: "Wrap body text around figures in Quarto"
toc: false
---

wrapped is a Quarto filter extension. It lets body text flow beside a
figure, to the left or right of it. The figure keeps its number, its
caption, and its `@fig-` links.

::: demo
This box shows the layout. The paragraph that you are reading comes before
the figure, so it runs the full width of the box.

![Mean ratings by condition.](images/ratings.png){#fig-home .wrap-right width="40%"}

This paragraph sits beside @fig-home. The figure has the class
`.wrap-right`, so it goes to the right side of the text column, and the
paragraphs after it flow on its left.

One markdown syntax gives this layout in HTML, in PDF through LaTeX, in
PDF through Typst, and in Word. The figure keeps its number and its
caption, and the text can point to it with a `@fig-` link, as the
paragraph before this one does. Its width is 40% of the text column,
which is the default. Each format draws the layout with its own tools:
CSS in HTML, wrapfig in LaTeX, wrap-it in Typst, and a frame in Word. The
text is not split into two columns. It flows beside the figure, and the
last lines of this paragraph run under the figure, at the full width of
the text. Wrapping stops at the next block that is not
a paragraph, such as a heading or a list. In a window 576px wide or
narrower, the figure stops floating and takes the full width of the text
column.
:::

This version wraps figures in HTML output, revealjs slides and dashboards
included, in PDF through LaTeX, in PDF through Typst, and in Word. In
every other format, a wrapped figure renders as a normal figure, and the
render prints one warning. A table with a `#tbl-` label wraps in HTML and
in PDF through Typst. In the other formats it keeps its normal layout,
and the render prints a warning.

## Install

The extension asks for Quarto 1.9.36 or later. Each change to it is tested
with Quarto 1.9.36 and with Quarto's current release. In the folder of your project, run:

```bash
quarto add jmgirard/wrapped
```

Then add the filter to the document's YAML header:

```yaml
filters:
  - wrapped
```

[Get started](get-started.qmd) shows each kind of figure that wraps. The
[examples](examples/index.qmd) show each one rendered in HTML, in PDF
through LaTeX, in PDF through Typst, and in Word.
